name: Mauritius
headline: Mauritius: +3.2% growth in 2025, 3.7% inflation, debt 87% of GDP
sections: Mauritius is a $16.1 billion economy (2025), the world's 145th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +3.2% in 2025, close to the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $34K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 11.2% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 3.7% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 10.8% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 5.7% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 17.4% (2025).
Gross government debt is 87% of GDP (2025), a elevated level that has fallen from 92% in 2020. The general government balance is −3.8% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −7.0% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Trade equals 140% of GDP (2025), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 5.0% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 89% of GDP by 2031, broadly stable from today's level. Life expectancy is 73.8 years (2024). Population: 1.2 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
